chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed his wealth in the way of Allah.
He said: 'Give it to the one he bequeathed it to, even if he were a Jew or a Christian.
Indeed, Allah the Exalted says: 'So whoever alters it after he has heard it, then the sin is only upon those who alter it.'"
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a bequest made to a non-Muslim in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that a bequest to 'the way of Allah' is fulfilled by giving the wealth to the specific individual named in the will, even if they are a Jew or Christian, thereby prioritizing the testator's explicit intent over a general religious category. This ruling is grounded in Surah al-Baqarah 2:181, which warns against altering a bequest after hearing it, emphasizing the sanctity of the deceased's final wishes. The implication is that the beneficiary's faith does not invalidate the bequest, as the obligation is to execute the will as stated, not to judge the recipient's piety.
